'''John Calvin Giddings''' (September 26, 1930 – October 24, 1996) was a Distinguished Professor of chemistry at the [[University of Utah]].<ref name="urlSpringerLink - Journal Article">{{cite journal |title=J. Calvin Giddings 1930-1996  |year=1996 |doi=10.1007/BF02292971 |last1=Myers |first1=Marcus |journal=Chromatographia |volume=43 |issue=11–12 |page=583 |s2cid=94891956 }} Obituary by Marcus Myers, ''Chromatographia 43'', (11-12), 583, 1996</ref><ref name="Deseret News">{{cite news |url=https://www.deseretnews.com/article/521564/DEATH--DR-J-CALVIN-GIDDINGS.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201042036/https://www.deseretnews.com/article/521564/DEATH--DR-J-CALVIN-GIDDINGS.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 1, 2017 |title=Death: Dr. J. Calvin Giddings |work=Deseret News |date=1996-10-27 |accessdate=2017-11-20 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=People: J. Calvin Giddings dies at 66|journal=Analytical Chemistry|volume=68|issue=23|year=1996|pages=718A–719A|issn=0003-2700|doi=10.1021/ac962152b|pmid=8946788|last1=Henry|first1=C. M.}}</ref> Giddings received a B.S. degree from [[Brigham Young University]] in 1952 and a PhD from the University of Utah in 1954.  Following [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral]] work at the University of Utah and the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin]], he joined the faculty of the University of Utah as assistant professor of chemistry in 1957.  He became associate professor in 1959, research professor in 1962, and professor in 1966. Giddings authored or co-authored more than 400 publications and edited 32 books in the field of chemistry. He was executive editor of the journal ''Separation Science and Technology'', and the editor of the series Advances in chromatography.<ref>{{cite web |title=J. Calvin Giddings papers |publisher=Archives West |url=https://archiveswest.orbiscascade.org/ark:/80444/xv23925/pdf |website=archiveswest.orbiscascade.org |access-date=13 October 2023}}{{PD-notice}}</ref>

Gidding's work in  separation sciences shed light on the chromatographic processes, as well as other separation techniques, including non-equilibrium,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Giddings |first=J. Calvin |date=1959-12-01 |title=Nonequilibrium Kinetics and Chromatography |url=https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1730636 |journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |volume=31 |issue=6 |pages=1462–1467 |doi=10.1063/1.1730636 |bibcode=1959JChPh..31.1462G |issn=0021-9606|url-access=subscription }}</ref> diffusion & eddy diffusion,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Giddings |first=J. Calvin |date= 1959|title='Eddy' Diffusion in Chromatography |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/184357a0 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=184 |issue=4683 |pages=357–358 |doi=10.1038/184357a0 |bibcode=1959Natur.184..357G |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref> pressure changes,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Giddings |first=J. Calvin |date= 1966|title=Some Aspects of Pressure-Induced Equilibrium Shifts in Chromatography |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/01496396608049435 |journal=Separation Science |language=en |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=73–80 |doi=10.1080/01496396608049435 |issn=0037-2366|url-access=subscription }}</ref> flow in paper and [[thin-layer chromatography]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Calvin Giddings |first1=J. |last2=A. Keller |first2=Roy |date=1959-01-01 |title=Spot Distribution and size in paper chromatography* |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0021967301863561 |journal=Journal of Chromatography A |volume=2 |pages=626–633 |doi=10.1016/S0021-9673(01)86356-1 |issn=0021-9673|url-access=subscription }}</ref> preparative-scale, and programmed-temperature [[Gas chromatography|gas chromatography (GC)]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Giddings |first=J. Calvin |date= 1962|title=Elementary theory of programed temperature gas chromatography |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ed039p569 |journal=Journal of Chemical Education |language=en |volume=39 |issue=11 |pages=569 |doi=10.1021/ed039p569 |bibcode=1962JChEd..39..569G |issn=0021-9584|url-access=subscription }}</ref> [[Size-exclusion chromatography|exclusion chromatography]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Giddings |first1=J. Calvin |last2=Kucera |first2=Eugene |last3=Russell |first3=Christopher Penn |last4=Myers |first4=Marcus N. |date= 1968|title=Statistical theory for the equilibrium distribution of rigid molecules in inert porous networks. Exclusion chromatography |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/j100859a008 |journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry |language=en |volume=72 |issue=13 |pages=4397–4408 |doi=10.1021/j100859a008 |issn=0022-3654|url-access=subscription }}</ref> [[electrophoresis]],<ref name="Giddings 1258A–1270A">{{Cite journal |last=Giddings |first=J. Calvin |date=1984-10-01 |title=Two-dimensional separations: concept and promise |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ac00276a003 |journal=Analytical Chemistry |language=en |volume=56 |issue=12 |pages=1258A–1270A |doi=10.1021/ac00276a003 |issn=0003-2700|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and the generation of non-gaussian zones.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Grushka |first1=Elimelech. |last2=Myers |first2=Marcus N. |last3=Giddings |first3=J. Calvin. |date=1970-01-01 |title=Moments analysis for the discernment of overlapping chromatographic peaks |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ac60283a015 |journal=Analytical Chemistry |language=en |volume=42 |issue=1 |pages=21–26 |doi=10.1021/ac60283a015 |issn=0003-2700|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He developed understanding of the optimization of multicomponent chromatography<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Giddings |first=J. Calvin |date=1995-06-26 |title=Sample dimensionality: A predictor of order-disorder in component peak distribution in multidimensional separation |url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/0021-9673%2895%2900249-M |journal=Journal of Chromatography A |volume=703 |issue=1 |pages=3–15 |doi=10.1016/0021-9673(95)00249-M |issn=0021-9673|url-access=subscription }}</ref> especially in 2D separations.<ref name="Giddings 1258A–1270A"/>

His vision of the capabilities of high-pressure chromatographic systems evolved into [[High-performance liquid chromatography|High Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC)]], by suggesting to reduce particle size of the columns' packing in liquid chromatography.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Giddings |first=J. C. |date=1963-12-01 |title=Liquid Chromatography with Operating Conditions Analogous to Those of Gas Chromatography. |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ac60206a063 |journal=Analytical Chemistry |language=en |volume=35 |issue=13 |pages=2215–2216 |doi=10.1021/ac60206a063 |issn=0003-2700|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Giddings also envisioned the capabilities of [[Supercritical fluid chromatography]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=DePalma |first=Angelo |title=INSIGHTS on Analytical Chromatography: New Kid on the Block |url=https://www.labmanager.com/new-kid-on-the-block-10423 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250814204848/https://www.labmanager.com/new-kid-on-the-block-10423 |archive-date=2025-08-14 |access-date=2026-02-13 |website=Lab Manager |language=en}}</ref> by developing the theory and ground work of dense gas chromatographic system.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=McLaren |first1=Lilian |last2=Myers |first2=Marcus N. |last3=Giddings |first3=J. Calvin |date=1968-01-12 |title=Dense-Gas Chromatography of Nonvolatile Substances of High Molecular Weight |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.159.3811.197 |journal=Science |language=en |volume=159 |issue=3811 |pages=197–199 |doi=10.1126/science.159.3811.197 |bibcode=1968Sci...159..197M |issn=0036-8075|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Eventually Prof Giddings invented the one-phase separation technique called "[[Field flow fractionation|field-flow fractionation]]" (FFF).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Giddings |first=J. Calvin |date= 1984|title=Field-Flow Fractionation |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/01496398408068596 |journal=Separation Science and Technology |language=en |volume=19 |issue=11–12 |pages=831–847 |doi=10.1080/01496398408068596 |issn=0149-6395|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>Giddings, J.C., Yang F.J., and Myers M.N. (1976). "Flow Field-Flow Fractionation: a versatile new separation method." Science 193.4259: 1244–1245.</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=75 years of Chromatography a Historical Dialogue |year=1979 |isbn=9780444417541 |series=Journal of Chromatography Library |volume=17 |pages=87–98 |chapter=J. Calvin Giddings |doi=10.1016/S0301-4770(08)60638-7 |issn=0301-4770}}</ref> He developed the concept of a chromatographic-like system in which retention is established and controlled by an external field rather than by the stationary phase. The FFF system extends the range of chromatography upward to include macromolecules and particles of almost every type and size, from 0.001 to 10 μm and beyond.

He was nominated for a Nobel Prize in 1984 and 1994.<ref name="Deseret News" />

Giddings received numerous honors for his work<ref name="Deseret News" /> including American Chemical Society Awards in Chromatography and Electrophoresis, in Analytical Chemistry, and in Separation Science and Technology. He also received the Tswett Medal in Chromatography, and the Nichols Medical from the New York Section of the ACS.  On May 27, 1987, Giddings received an [[Honorary degree|honorary doctorate]] from the faculty of pharmacy at [[Uppsala University]], [[Sweden]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uu.se/en/about-uu/traditions/prizes/honorary-doctorates/|title=Honorary doctorates – Uppsala University, Sweden|website=www.uu.se}}</ref>

He died of cancer in 1996.<ref name="Deseret News" />

==Selected works==
* J. Calvin Giddings (1965). ''Dynamics of Chromatography''. Marcel Decker, NY.
* J. Calvin Giddings (1991). ''Unified Separation Science''. [[Wiley (publisher)|John Wiley & Sons]], NY.
